# The agent

You are a Seon agent: you work one task at a Clojure REPL on your own branch, and every change you make is a form you evaluate.

This page is what every agent reads first, and `(my.agent/help)` lists its sections again; `(my.agent/help "done")` shows one whole. Every single-backticked form on it runs in an agent as written (`seon.repl-test/the-help-page-runs`); a double-backticked one is a pattern to fill in.

## Your turn

You have one tool, eval: call it with Clojure forms, and you see what the REPL answered before your next call.

- Evaluate a little, read the answer, then take the next step. Prose inside your code goes in `;;` comments, and text outside an eval call is never evaluated.
- Identical forms with identical answers are folded into one, headed by how many times they repeated (`;; 24x`).
- An unbalanced delimiter is repaired, and the repair is shown to you next turn under `:your-last-reply`, as is a reply cut at the model's token limit.
- Every cut in what you read names the form that reads its rest. Your last turn's evaluations in full: `(my.turn/evals)`.

## What you read

Your context comes in two parts: the run's, sent once and unchanged while you work, then the turn's, measured again after each of your replies.

The run's part:
- `:task`: its id, kind and instructions, and its plan as it accumulated along its needs, prerequisites first.
- `:references`: each var the plan cites, at the depth its delimiter asks (`docs/references.md#the-delimiter-picks-the-depth`): a bare name its arglists and first sentence, one backtick its doc and contract, three its source. A source past the cap shows `:left-out` and `:read`, the form that reads it.
- `:found`: program functions the cited vars and your proofs call that the plan does not name, and the program forms nearest the plan in meaning; often the helpers the task needs.
- `:map`: the functions of the namespaces your proofs and cited vars live in, a line each (name, arglists, first sentence), most used first; ``(clojure.repl/dir the.ns)`` lists them all. Before writing a helper, look here for one.
- `:sections`: the wiki sections, files and namespaces the plan cites, at their depth.
- `:evidence`: why the last run on this branch was refused (`:problem`) and what it measured: conflicts, unmerged keys, red proofs. Root held the task and released it again here, on the same branch, so its work is yours to continue.

The turn's part:
- `:turn`: this turn of the most you have.
- `:proofs`: each of your proofs and its status. A red one shows each failure as `:assert` (as written) and `:got` (what it evaluated to), its source, and `:calls`, the program functions it calls. `:undefined` is not written yet, `:not-run` means the test run failed (see `:test-run`), `:no-assertions` means it ran and asserted nothing.
- `:refused`: what keeps you from done beyond your red proofs (the done rule, `seon.reconcile/done-explain`): `:regression` (green on main, red here: your change broke it), `:stray-red` (a red test that is no task's proof), `:contract-gap` (a function you defined without a ``:malli/schema``), `:open-problem` (a problem your own work made true, such as a citation of a var you deleted: `seon.problems/caused`), `:proof-unknown` (a proof with no result: it never ran), `:unmerged` (a merge entry not resolved), `:no-proofs`, and on a design task `:no-design` (your plan is unchanged since the run began; it shows the form that changes it).
- `:test-run`: the test run itself failing (a timeout, a dead fork); no test result is real until it runs.
- `:unmerged`: on a merge task, the entries to resolve.
- `:attention`: the wiki sections your code changes made stale, to read and probably fix; never a reason to refuse done.
- `:will-merge`: every change your branch's merge will carry to main: the vars you added, changed and removed, and the schemas you registered or changed; `{}` when it carries nothing. Anything listed that the task does not need, put back.
- `:tests`: how many tests this turn ran (`:this-turn`: your proofs and the tests your branch changed), how many root's judge runs at your run's end (`:at-judge`, `(my.agent/prove)` runs the same), and `:when-asked`: tests your change reaches that start a process of their own (a shell, a fork, a root). Those never run in your turn or the judge unless one is a proof of your task; root runs the others when it asks. `(my.agent/deferred)` lists them.
- `:messages`: what was sent to you since your last turn, each `{:from :body}`: the owner's words (`:from "owner"`), root's, or another agent's (its run id). The owner's is a fact (`:seon.message/*`) your turn writes on your branch, and every later reading of the turn reads it again from that commit.
- Your last evaluations, when no earlier turn shows them.

## The REPL

This is a real Clojure REPL: what you define becomes part of your branch's program exactly as written.

- Your work is Clojure forms evaluated here. Think in `;;` comments right before each form: what it is for, what you expect it to show. The comments are recorded with the form's evaluation (a definition keeps them as its leading comment), and the owner reads them beside each form and its result. The eval tool's optional `thinking` says why the whole call.

- `(ns app.workout)` creates a namespace (with its `:require`s) and it becomes part of your program; ``(in-ns 'the.ns)`` then ``(defn f ...)`` changes an existing one, and its callers see it at once.
- Every function you define needs a Malli contract in its metadata: `(defn total {:malli/schema [:=> [:cat [:vector :int]] :int]} [xs] (reduce + 0 xs))`.
- Your own namespace is scratch and never merges: `(in-ns (symbol (str "agent." (name (:id (my.agent/whoami))))))`. There the `my.*` functions are referred unqualified; elsewhere call them qualified, as written here.
- A schema changes as a function does, on your branch: `(my.schema/register! :app.workout/set [:map [:reps :int] [:kg :double]])`; your next forms see it. To change an existing key, start from its form: `(get (my.schema/forms) :seon.task/task)`.
- Your branch's program is the forms you evaluate, recorded on your branch; the files in the checkout are not your branch. Writing a file under src or test, or running git, changes the shared checkout under every agent and root, not your program: a file is an effect, through its owner.
- An earlier result: ``(my.agent/$ :h3)`` by its handle, or `*1`; the last error is `*e`, and ``(my.agent/pst)`` prints it with its causes.

## Finding your way

The program as your branch records it answers where things are, so read before you write.

- By name: `(clojure.repl/apropos "accumulate")`; by docstring: `(clojure.repl/find-doc "accumulated plan")`; by the text of a definition: `(my.agent/grep "accumulated")`.
- A function: `(clojure.repl/doc seon.task/accumulate)` and `(clojure.repl/source seon.task/accumulate)`; who calls it: `(my.agent/callers 'seon.task/accumulate)`; what it calls: `(my.agent/callees 'seon.task/accumulate)`.
- A namespace's ns form, its requires and aliases (to write a test where its siblings are): `(clojure.repl/source seon.task)`.
- A namespace's publics: `(clojure.repl/dir my.task)`; every program namespace: `(my.db/q '[:find [?n ...] :where [_ :ns/name ?n]])`.
- Your task: `(my.task/current)`; one task by id: `(seon.task/task (my.db/db) (:seon.task/id (my.task/current)))`.
- An effect (a file, a model, git) goes through its owner: ``(my.fx/call :kind req)``.

## Done

Your task is done when every proof passes and the done rule refuses nothing; the proofs run after each of your replies. A run that ends refused (a red or unrun proof, a reason, no progress, a dead agent, a refused merge) is not retried: its task is held for root, which decides whether to run it again (`docs/tasks.md#a-refused-run-is-held-for-root`).

- A proof is a deftest in a test namespace: `(ns app.workout-test (:require [clojure.test :refer [deftest is]] [app.workout :as w]))`, then `(deftest total-sums (is (= 6 (w/total [1 2 3]))))`, run with `(clojure.test/run-tests 'app.workout-test)`.
- A cost proof (`seon.cost/proof`) is your performance goal: it says what N counts, the least work the data needs (`:work`, e.g. one pass with one lookup per row), how that grows and what it may cost. Read it before writing code and do no more work than it states.
- Run what judges your branch now, as root's judge does: ``(my.agent/prove)`` runs your proofs and every test your change reaches, reusing each one green at its reach digest, and answers `:results`.
- The judge counts exactly (`seon.cost/slack`): allocated bytes may reach 1.25x the estimate, contracted calls 1.0x and ticks (the counted time dimension) 3x. CPU time (`:ns`) is measured and shown ("TIME OVER") but never red. A dimension whose growth exponent exceeds `:growth`'s by more than `seon.cost/steeper-by` (0.3) is STEEPER (an extra pass), red even inside the slack; LOOSE (a third of the estimate or less) is not red. Its failure message prints measured over estimate per size.

## Merging

A merge task's branch has main merged in, and each of its unmerged entries shows `:base`, `:ours` and `:theirs`.

- `(my.branch/unmerged)` lists them. Resolve one by redefining the var with the content both sides need, or keep one side: ``(my.branch/resolve! 'ns/var :theirs)``, or ``(my.branch/resolve! 'ns/var)`` to keep yours.
- Your branch sees only its own changes until then.

## Ending

Record what you learned in the plan, so the next step starts from it, then stop.

- `(my.task/update! :seon.task/plan str "\n\nFound: seon.task/accumulate owns the plan's accumulation.")`.
- When the task cannot be done as planned, fail it with the form that shows why: `(my.task/fail! "the premise is refuted" '(seon.task/accumulate {} "x"))`. The failure goes on the task, your run ends, and the task is held for root (`docs/tasks.md#a-refused-run-is-held-for-root`).
- `(my.turn/wait)` ends your turn and waits for root.

{:printed "nil",
 :form "(clojure.repl/source seon.context/callees)",
 :out
   "(defn callees
  \"The program functions proof p calls directly (one level: its recorded form's :form/refs,
  the compiler's resolved references), each at summary level from its own facts on db: its
  contract and doc, never its body; a var is program when db holds it (a branch's callee
  this process never loaded included).\"
  {:malli/schema [:=> [:cat :seon.host/db :qualified-symbol] [:vector :map]]}
  [db p]
  (vec (for [q (sort (disj (set (d/q '[:find [?r ...] :in $ ?s :where [?e :var/name ?s] [?e :var/form ?f] [?f :form/refs ?r]] db p)) p))
             :let [v (d/entity db [:var/name q])]
             :when (and v (not= :test (:var/kind v)))]
         (cond-> {:var q}
           (:var/contract v) (assoc :contract (clojure.edn/read-string (:var/contract v)))
           (:var/doc v) (assoc :doc (:var/doc v))))))
"}

  [sym]
  (vec (sort (disj (set (d/q '[:find [?r ...] :in $ ?s :where [?e :var/name ?s] [?e :var/form ?f] [?f :form/refs ?r]]
                             (agent/db) sym))
                   sym))))
"}

{:printed "nil",
 :form "(clojure.repl/source seon.context/current-state)",
 :out
   "(defn current-state
  \"The current-state block of task t as data: proofs with their status, red assertions and
  source; what else the done rule refuses (regressions, stray reds, contract gaps), and a
  test run that failed as a whole; resolved references, each at its citation's depth; the
  helpers the plan does not name (:found); the measured evidence it starts from; the
  branch's unmerged entries (base, ours, theirs); what its merge will carry to main; what
  happened to the last reply; the messages delivered since the last turn (the owner's, root's,
  other agents'); the last evaluations; turns left.\"
  {:malli/schema [:=> [:cat :seon.host/db :seon.task/task :map] :map]}
  [db t {:keys [results reds last-items turn max-turns unmerged truncated? reasons test-run-errors source repairs will-merge tests messages message-ids attention]}]
  (let [{:keys [plan proofs]} (:seon.task/accumulated t)
        cites (ref/references db (str plan \"\\n\" (:seon.task/instructions t)))
        refs (filterv #(= :var (docs/citation-kind db %)) cites)
        named (into (set proofs) (map :seon.ref/name) refs)
        helpers (found db named (into (mapv :seon.ref/name refs) (sort-by str proofs)) (some->> (:seon.task/id t) (pdb/eid db :seon.task/id)))
        nsmap (ns-map db (into (vec (sort-by str proofs)) (map :seon.ref/name) refs))
        sections (into [] (comp (filter #(= :view (docs/citation-kind db %))) (map #(docs/cited-view db %)))
                       cites)]
    (cond-> {:task (assoc (select-keys t [:seon.task/id :seon.task/kind :seon.task/instructions])
                          ;; the plan as it accumulated along :needs (prerequisites first)
                          :seon.task/plan plan)
             ;; a passing proof is its status; a red or unrun one shows its source, its failures
             ;; and the program functions it calls; one not defined yet says so
             :proofs (vec (for [p (sort-by str proofs)
                                :let [src (docs/source-of db p)
                                      ;; no result: not written yet, the run failed as a whole, or it asserted nothing
                                      st (get results p (cond (nil? src) :undefined (seq test-run-errors) :not-run :else :no-assertions))
                                      fs (filter #(= p (:test %)) reds)]]
                            (cond-> {:test p :status st}
                              (and src (not= :pass st)) (assoc :source src)
                              (seq fs) (assoc :failures (mapv failure fs))
                              (and src (not= :pass st) (seq (callees db p))) (assoc :calls (callees db p)))))
             ;; a reference already shown as a proof is not shown twice; the names that resolve
             ;; to nothing are one entry, their problem said once
             :references (let [rs (into [] (comp (remove (comp (set proofs) :seon.ref/name))
                                                 (map #(docs/resolve-ref db (:seon.ref/name %) (:seon.ref/depth %))))
                                        refs)
                               {gone true there false} (group-by (comp boolean :unresolved) rs)]
                           (cond-> (vec there)
                             gone (conj {:unresolved (mapv :symbol gone) :problem (:unresolved ref/problem-messages)})))}
      max-turns (assoc :turn (str (inc turn) \" of \" max-turns))
      (seq sections) (assoc :sections sections)
      (seq helpers) (assoc :found helpers)
      (seq nsmap) (assoc :map nsmap)
      (seq (refused (vec reasons) (vec reds))) (assoc :refused (refused (vec reasons) (vec reds)))
      (seq test-run-errors) (assoc :test-run {:failed (vec test-run-errors)})
      (last-reply truncated? source (vec repairs)) (assoc :your-last-reply (last-reply truncated? source (vec repairs)))
      (:seon.task/evidence t) (assoc :evidence (:seon.task/evidence t))
      (seq unmerged) (assoc :unmerged (mapv #(select-keys % [:key :kind :base :ours :theirs]) unmerged))
      ;; owner D4: every change the branch's merge carries to main, every turn
      ;; measured and empty ({}) says so; absent only when not measured (a basis before D4)
      ;; the sections of the wiki this branch's code changes made stale (seon.problems/caused-split): to read and
      ;; probably fix; never a reason to refuse done
      (seq attention) (assoc :attention attention)
      (some? will-merge) (assoc :will-merge will-merge)
      ;; the messages the turn took: those that are facts read again from db (the commit the turn
      ;; read, where its agent wrote them), the rest as the basis holds them
      (or (seq message-ids) (seq messages))
      (assoc :messages (mapv #(dissoc % :id) (taken-messages db {:message-ids message-ids :messages messages})))
      ;; root's ruling (a): the tests this turn ran (the proofs and the tests the
      ;; branch changed), those the judge runs at the run's end, the process tests run only
      ;; when root asks (DECISIONS, Process tests are not automatic); a run its bound ended leaves
      ;; the rest unknown, never red
      tests (assoc :tests (cond-> tests
                            (:unfinished tests) (assoc :unfinished-run '(my.agent/prove))
                            (pos? (:at-judge tests 0)) (assoc :judge-runs '(my.agent/prove))
                            (pos? (:when-asked tests 0)) (assoc :root-runs '(my.agent/deferred))))
      (seq last-items) (assoc :last-evals (transcript (fold-evals last-items))))))
"}
